comparison: Perfect match on C44-C45 regarding tumor growth inhibition via BMT. Both evaluations find the data SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed statistical analysis (p<0.03, p<0.001), while peer reviewers accept the BMT data without specific challenge.

Perfect match on C4, C46, C75-C77 regarding NK cell cytotoxicity and importance. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with detailed statistical evidence, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting the mechanism remains unresolved and unclear whether NK cells or PD-1/PDL-1 modulation is primarily involved.

Perfect match on C6, C65-C74, C91-C92 regarding proteomics analysis. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with acknowledgment that causal inference is speculative. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating the authors make broad inferences beyond the data and claims are overstated.

Strong match on C62-C64 regarding cytokine expression (IL-4, IL-6). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED noting the inference is correlative rather than causative. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, treating these as secondary supporting data without specific challenge.

Strong match on C5, C50-C60 regarding PD-1/PDL-1 expression and regulation. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED noting the exact mechanism requires validation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, emphasizing that ChIP data shows similar binding of WT and K74R EKLF, leaving the mechanism unclear.

Strong match on C3, C31-C40 regarding BMT transfer of anti-cancer capability. Both evaluations rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed dose-response analysis, peer reviewers accept the transferability without challenge.

Match on C86, C93 regarding translational potential and anti-disease/anti-aging claims. Both rate UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes these are aspirational goals not demonstrated results. Peer reviewers state there is no evidence for broad anti-disease/anti-aging effects, only resistance to specific cancer models.

Partial match on C2, C22-C23, C25-C26 regarding background/age/sex independence. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval covers broader claims including homozygosity and K74A data. Peer reviewers focus on the expanded model validation.

Partial match on C24, C27-C28 regarding homozygosity requirement and K74A substitution. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval groups these with broader anti-cancer effects, peer reviewers acknowledge without challenge.

Partial match on C29-C30 regarding hepatocellular carcinoma model. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval includes this in broader anti-cancer characterization, peer reviewers specifically note the second cancer model strengthens the data.

Partial match on C85 regarding lifespan extension. Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes minor discrepancy in reported values and correlative nature of ICG inference. Peer reviewers accept the finding but note it is incremental.

Partial match on C90 regarding ICG contribution. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED noting correlative relationship. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN as part of broader mechanistic uncertainty about transcriptional differences.

Partial match on C87 regarding transcriptional changes mechanism. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with caveat that exact molecular mechanism needs investigation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, stating the mechanism remains unclear with insufficient evidence.

Partial match on C47-C49 regarding EKLF expression in immune cells. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as part of broader PD-1/PDL-1 regulation evidence. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning cell-intrinsic effects given extremely low EKLF expression in T and B cells.

Partial match on C41-C42 regarding lifespan extension via BMT. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with detailed survival analysis. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED but note the finding is incremental compared to previous work.

OpenEval R1 covers C1, C17-C21, C94-C96 regarding basic characterization of Klf1(K74R) model from prior work, rated SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/foundational claims.

OpenEval R11 covers C7-C16, C82-C84, C88-C89, C97-C100 regarding background/context claims from published literature, rated SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature-based foundational claims.

Peer review R9 addresses C47-C49 regarding EKLF expression levels in immune cells, rated UNCERTAIN due to extremely low expression raising questions about cell-intrinsic effects. While OpenEval R6 includes these claims, the peer review focuses specifically on the expression level concern not emphasized in OpenEval's evaluation.
